title: Head of Deployment
leads: The operators and site leads in your book of sites, and every new site's team on launch day.
where: New sites in launch weeks, and the sites in your book the rest of the time

posting.headline: Head of Deployment (new sites and training), Cairo
posting.about: We run video recording teams at factories, warehouses, farms, and construction sites across Cairo. Workers wear a small camera on a cap while they do their normal job. The Head of Deployment opens every new site: launch day with the Portfolio Manager, and the first-day lesson for new operators, site leads, and Portfolio Managers. You also run a book of sites.
do: Run launch day: charging stations, labels, network test, first lesson, pilot recordings.
Collect the kit from the store on launch morning. Hand it to the Portfolio Manager. Count it together. Both sign.
Own the first-day lessons for operators, site leads, and Portfolio Managers. Keep them current.
Give every new Portfolio Manager the first lesson before they take a book.
Run your own book of sites and reach its monthly hour target.
Hand your book to the first new Portfolio Manager on their day one. Then you hold Deployment and training only.
need: You have run a floor: a factory, a warehouse, or a site.
Able to teach a job in plain words and check that it stuck.
Careful with a list. Every phone, every count, every signature.
On your feet across Cairo, six days a week.
plus: You have been an operator or a Portfolio Manager with us.
You have opened a new site or a new shift somewhere before.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
Your first launch with the Director of Operations beside you.
A clear procedure for launch day.
You are the named deputy of the Director of Operations.
posting.apply: Send your name, age, where you live, a phone number, and the floors you have run. We call back within two working days.

paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Head of Deployment at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the Director of Operations.
Your start date is {start}. You run your first launch day with {manager} beside you.

handbook.purpose: The client pays for accepted hours. A new site's hours start on a launch day that went right: a whole kit, a tested line, trained operators, clean pilots. You make that day happen at every new site, and you teach the job to everyone who joins the floor. You keep a book of running sites for September, until the first new Portfolio Manager takes it.
outcomes: Every new site launches on the day named, with a whole kit and trained operators.
Every phone you hand over is counted, signed for, and on the map.
Every new operator, site lead, and Portfolio Manager gets the first lesson and passes it.
Your book of sites reaches its monthly target, until you hand it over.
daily: 7:00 AM. Clock in with your sites. Visit them without warning during the shift.
A launch date lands. Get the site plan and the kit list from the Planning and Logistics Lead. Walk the site once before launch day.
Launch days. Count the kit, test the line, train, check every pilot, get Moharam's yes.
6:00 PM. Check the daily report form from each site lead in your book.
weekly: Thursday, 4:00 PM. The three-way count: registry, MDM, and room say the same number.
Once a week. Next week's launches with the Planning and Logistics Lead. A kit that will be short means the date waits.
monthly: Review the month's launches with Moharam: what was short, what moved, what to change.
standards: No site launches short. A kit is whole, or launch day moves.
A phone joins a launch only after it shows on the map and has uploaded a test.
Nobody signs for a count that is not their count.
Nothing written on the outside of a bag.
Nothing records for real before Moharam certifies the launch.
The handover rule: when the first new Portfolio Manager signs off on day one, your book goes to them the same day. You hold Deployment and training only.
Gear through the Planning and Logistics Lead, money to Ahmed Alaa, quality to Youssef Medhat. Nobody contacts the client.
never: A kit filled from another site's kit.
A phone that goes home, or an account that is shared, ends the job.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: In the store with the Planning and Logistics Lead. The registry, the kit list, the tags.
Walk one site plan end to end with the Planning and Logistics Lead. Count one kit before the handover, with Moharam.
Run one launch day with Moharam there. Train the operators. Check every pilot.
Your own book of sites. Two daily reports accepted in a row. Moharam signs you off.

measures: Launches on the day the schedule named, with a whole kit.
Phones handed over already on the map, with a test uploaded.
New operators, site leads, and Portfolio Managers who passed the first lesson.
Accepted hours in your book, against the monthly target.
handbook.call: Moharam, for the floor or a launch that will not hold. The Planning and Logistics Lead for the kit, the store, or the registry. Youssef Medhat for a pilot. Ahmed Alaa for money. A missing bag: Moharam now.
